children: Taiwan will ban short-selling any stock trading below its previous close from Monday, its third move against short sellers this month after two earlier attempts failed to stop the market slide. The restriction was announced Saturday, according to BeInCrypto, and also requires short sellers to post more collateral and asks lenders to stop lending shares; securities and futures firms hedging business positions are exempt.

Taiwan’s tech-heavy market fell almost 18% last week, while South Korea’s KOSPI lost about 8%. On Friday, the Taiex dropped 6.2% to its lowest close in nearly seven months, marking its third-biggest one-day point loss ever. The decline followed concerns that heavy investment in AI may not pay off, and Nvidia’s better-than-expected earnings on November 17 did not halt the slide. Taiwan’s $15 billion state stabilization fund said it has bought shares since November 6 and that foreign selling has eased. Barclays said retail investors facing margin calls added to the November 16 sell-off. The government says Taiwan’s fundamentals remain strong, while a local asset manager expects a rebound when panic fades. Monday’s open will be the first test of the restriction.

title: Taiwan Restricts Short-Selling as AI-Linked Market Selloff Deepens
